markdown:
## Bottom line
**Suggests Normal (100%)** · Confident · Read in turn
Conformal set, second model and all 5 similar cases agree [F1].

## Confidence
| Signal | Value | Reading |
|---|---|---|
| Top probabilities | Normal 100%; others <1% | One dominant class |
| Conformal set | {Normal} at 90% | Single class |
| Reliability / OOD | 0.98 / 14th percentile | Typical, good-quality image |
| Second-model (MUSK) agreement | Same top class | Independent model concurs |
| Similar cases | 5/5 Normal | Neighbours agree |

## Tissue evidence
- **Benign fibrous stroma or fat** (regions 0, 5, 6) · ↓ invasive · Prominent benign stroma; scored above typical [F3] · Validated
- **Normal lobules with two-layered epithelium** (regions 1, 4, 5) · ↓ invasive · Scored above typical; AI spot check 0/20 [F2] · Unreliable
- **Dense lymphocytic infiltrate** (region 9) · context · Scored below typical; descriptive only [F4] · Weak

## Trust check
- **Heatmap**: Removing the top 3 regions drops the invasive logit 0.54 more than random (CI 0.47–0.60); faithful to the classifier.
- **Concepts**: Deletion CI includes 0 (+0.002; −0.005 to 0.007), so unproven; this case leans on the Unreliable normal-lobules concept.

## Could be wrong if
- Calibration rests on 132 test images (ECE 0.05, CI 0.03–0.18); treat 100% as approximate.
- Too few tumor nuclei were found for cell measurements, so no cell-level evidence corroborates this call.

## Check on the slide
1. **Regions 1, 4, 5:** Confirm two-layered lobular epithelium; this concept failed its AI spot check.
2. **Region 9:** Strongest lymphocyte, invasion and tubule scores; confirm four HoVer-Net "neoplastic" nuclei are benign.
3. **Region 10:** Necrosis-concept peak (unreliable); HoVer-Net labelled five nuclei dead. Check for true necrosis.
